questions.question:
Convert the interrogative sentence into Indirect Speech:
The supervisor said to the typist, "Can you complete this confidential tabulation today?"

options.text: The supervisor asked the typist if could he complete that confidential tabulation that day.
The supervisor asked the typist if he could complete that confidential tabulation that day.
The supervisor asked that if he could complete this confidential tabulation today.
The supervisor told the typist whether he can complete that confidential tabulation that day.

questions.explanation: Yes/No question modal 'Can' se shuru ho raha hai. Reporting verb 'said to' ➔ 'asked the typist'. Connective 'if' lagaya gaya. Modal 'can' backshift hokar 'could' bana aur subject 'he' ke BAAD shift hua ('if he could complete'). Demonstrative 'this' ➔ 'that' aur time adverbial 'today' ➔ 'that day' convert hua. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein inversion 'could he' retain hai. Option (C) mein 'that if' double conjunction hai aur time/place expressions unshifted hain. Option (D) mein reporting verb 'told' aur unbackshifted 'can' dono errors hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Yes/No Question with modal backshift and inversion removal.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Yes/No Question with 'Have' Auxiliary (Present Perfect ➔ Past Perfect)
questions.question:
Select the correct Indirect form:
The advocate said to the client, "Have you deposited the requisite court fee in the registry?"

options.text: The advocate asked the client whether he has deposited the requisite court fee in the registry.
The advocate asked the client whether he had deposited the requisite court fee in the registry.
The advocate asked the client that whether had he deposited the requisite court fee in the registry.
The advocate enquired the client if he had deposited the requisite court fee in the registry.

questions.explanation: Present Perfect question 'Have you deposited' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had deposited' banega. Subject 'he' auxiliary 'had' se pehle aayega ('whether he had deposited'). Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein 'has' ko backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (C) mein 'that whether' double conjunction aur 'had he' inverted order dono galat hain. Option (D) mein 'enquired' ke baad preposition 'of' missing hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Present Perfect interrogative shifts to Past Perfect with whether/if.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate Indirect Speech version:
The registrar said to the petitioner, "Will you argue the matter yourself or engage a counsel?"

options.text: The registrar asked the petitioner if he will argue the matter himself or engage a counsel.
The registrar asked the petitioner that whether he would argue the matter himself or engage a counsel.
The registrar enquired of the petitioner whether he would argue the matter himself or engage a counsel.
The registrar asked the petitioner whether would he argue the matter himself or engage a counsel.

questions.explanation: Explicit two-way alternative choice ('argue yourself OR engage a counsel') mein 'whether' sabse preferred aur accurate connective hota hai. Reporting clause mein 'enquired of the petitioner' bilkul correct prepositional concord follow karta hai. Modal 'will' backshift hokar 'would' bana aur subject 'he' ke baad aaya. Reflexive pronoun 'yourself' ➔ 'himself' bana. Option (C) 100% correct hai. Option (A) mein 'if' and unshifted 'will' dono weak hain. Option (B) mein 'that whether' double conjunction blunder hai. Option (D) mein 'would he' inversion retain hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02 & RC-04: Explicit alternative choice with 'whether... or' and 'enquired of'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the question into Indirect Speech:
The receptionist said to the visitor, "What is your roll number for the verification?"

options.text: The receptionist asked the visitor what was his roll number for the verification.
The receptionist asked the visitor what his roll number was for the verification.
The receptionist asked the visitor that what his roll number was for the verification.
The receptionist asked to the visitor what his roll number was for the verification.

questions.explanation: Wh-word 'what' connective banega. Quoted clause ka subject 'your roll number' 2nd person listener visitor ke anusaar 'his roll number' banega. Auxiliary 'is' backshift hokar 'was' banegi aur subject ke BAAD aayegi: 'what his roll number was for the verification'. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein auxiliary 'was' subject se pehle hi chhod di gayi hai ('what was his roll number') jo inversion blunder hai. Option (C) mein 'that what' double conjunction hai. Option (D) mein 'asked to the visitor' incorrect preposition use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Wh-questions place auxiliary verb after the entire noun phrase subject.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Wh-Question (When) with Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect
questions.question:
Identify the correct Indirect conversion:
The officer said to the clerk, "When did you dispatch the summoning notice?"

options.text: The officer asked the clerk when did he dispatch the summoning notice.
The officer asked the clerk when he had dispatched the summoning notice.
The officer asked the clerk when he dispatched the summoning notice.
The officer asked that when he had dispatched the summoning notice.

questions.explanation: Wh-word 'when' connective retain hoga. Simple Past question ('did dispatch') backshift hokar Past Perfect ('had dispatched') banega, aur subject 'he' auxiliary se pehle aayega. Option (B) bilkul correct hai. Option (A) mein question structure 'did he dispatch' retain hai. Option (C) mein Simple Past ko Past Perfect mein backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (D) mein 'that when' double conjunction blunder hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Wh-questions with Simple Past shift to Past Perfect without inversion.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert into Indirect Speech:
The magistrate said to the investigating officer, "How can you substantiate these allegations?"

options.text: The magistrate asked the investigating officer how could he substantiate those allegations.
The magistrate asked the investigating officer that how he could substantiate those allegations.
The magistrate asked the investigating officer how he could substantiate those allegations.
The magistrate enquired the investigating officer how he could substantiate these allegations.

questions.explanation: Wh-word 'how' connective banega. 2nd person 'you' officer ke anusaar 'he' banega. Modal 'can' backshift hokar 'could' banega aur subject 'he' ke baad aayega ('how he could substantiate'). Demonstrative 'these' ➔ 'those' banega. Option (C) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein inverted order 'could he' retain hai. Option (B) mein 'that how' double conjunction error hai. Option (D) mein 'enquired' ke baad 'of' missing hai aur 'these' unshifted hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: 'How' question with modal backshift and demonstrative shift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Select the correct Indirect form:
The head clerk said, "Who authorized the entry of this unauthorized person yesterday?"

options.text: The head clerk enquired who had authorized the entry of that unauthorized person the previous day.
The head clerk enquired who authorized the entry of this unauthorized person yesterday.
The head clerk asked that who had authorized the entry of that unauthorized person the previous day.
The head clerk enquired who did authorize the entry of that unauthorized person the previous day.

questions.explanation: 'Who' yahan khud sentence ka subject hai. Simple Past verb 'authorized' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had authorized' banegi. Demonstrative 'this' ➔ 'that' aur time adverbial 'yesterday' ➔ 'the previous day' convert hoga. Option (A) 100% accurate hai. Option (B) mein na tense backshift hua aur na hi time/place markers badle. Option (C) mein 'that who' double conjunction hai. Option (D) mein emphatic 'did authorize' ungrammatical hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Subject Wh-questions (Who + V2) convert to (Who + had + V3).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Inversion Spotting & Error Correction in Reported Questions
questions.question: Find the grammatically CORRECT sentence among the following options:

options.text: She enquired of the attendant where was the library situated.
She enquired of the attendant where the library was situated.
She enquired the attendant where the library was situated.
She enquired of the attendant that where was the library situated.

questions.explanation: Option (B) bilkul flawless hai: 'enquired of + listener object' bilkul sahi preposition leta hai, 'where' single connective hai, aur subject 'the library' auxiliary 'was' se pehle aaya hai ('where the library was situated'). Option (A) mein inversion 'was the library' galat hai. Option (C) mein 'enquired' ke baad 'of' missing hai. Option (D) mein 'that where' double conjunction aur inversion dono blunders hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03 & RC-04: Statement word order in reported clauses with enquired of.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Punctuation & Syntax Concord in Reported Questions
questions.question: Which of the following indirect sentences violates the punctuation and word-order rules of Narration?

options.text: The candidate asked whether the test commenced at nine o'clock.
The officer wanted to know why the server was offline.
The lawyer asked the client why had he concealed the second document?
The judge asked the witness how far he was from the scene.

questions.explanation: Option (C) do critical rules violate karta hai: (1) Isme inverted auxiliary order 'why had he concealed' use kiya gaya hai ('why he had concealed' hona chahiye tha); (2) End mein question mark (?) lagaya gaya hai, jabki indirect reported speech hamesha full stop (.) par end hoti hai. Baaki teeno options (A, B, D) bilkul correct indirect statements hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01 & RC-03: Indirect sentences require full stop and declarative word order.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate reporting verb for the sentence:
The Chief Justice said to the staff, "Maintain strict discipline and punctuality in all court departments."

options.text: The Chief Justice requested the staff to maintain strict discipline and punctuality...
The Chief Justice asked to the staff to maintain strict discipline and punctuality...
The Chief Justice ordered the staff to maintain strict discipline and punctuality...
The Chief Justice advised to the staff to maintain strict discipline and punctuality...

questions.explanation: Head of the institution (Chief Justice) administrative staff ko authoritative direction de rahe hain, isliye reporting verb 'ordered' (ya 'directed') sabse accurate context reflect karta hai. 'Ordered' transitive verb hai jo listener 'the staff' ko directly bina preposition ke leta hai, aur main verb 'maintain' ban jati hai 'to maintain'. Option (C) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) inappropriate 'requested' use karta hai. Option (B) aur (D) dono 'asked to' aur 'advised to' likhkar non-standard prepositional structure create karte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Hierarchical commands require 'ordered/directed + object + to + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Reporting Verb Selection for Moral / Legal Advice
questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Indirect Speech:
The senior counsel said to the junior, "Always cross-check the statutory amendments before filing."

options.text: The senior counsel ordered the junior to always cross-check the statutory amendments before filing.
The senior counsel advised the junior to always cross-check the statutory amendments before filing.
The senior counsel requested the junior to always cross-check the statutory amendments before filing.
The senior counsel told to the junior that always cross-check the statutory amendments before filing.

questions.explanation: Professional guidance aur practice recommendation ke context mein reporting verb 'advised' (ya 'counselled') sabse suitable hota hai. Structure 'advised + object + to + V1' ('advised the junior to always cross-check') bilkul standard hai. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein professional guidance ko authoritarian 'ordered' bana diya gaya. Option (C) mein 'requested' inappropriate hai. Option (D) mein fatal 'told to' aur incorrect 'that' structure hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Professional advice commands require 'advised + object + to + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Request with Pronoun and Time Reference Shift
questions.question:
Convert the request into Indirect Speech:
The clerk said to the superintendent, "Kindly grant me casual leave tomorrow."

options.text: The clerk requested the superintendent to kindly grant him casual leave tomorrow.
The clerk requested the superintendent to grant him casual leave the next day.
The clerk requested to the superintendent to grant him casual leave the next day.
The clerk ordered the superintendent to grant him casual leave the following day.

questions.explanation: 'Kindly' word polite request indicate karta hai, isliye reporting verb 'requested' aayegi aur 'kindly' drop ho jayega. 1st person 'me' clerk ke anusaar 'him' banega, verb 'grant' banegi 'to grant', aur 'tomorrow' banega 'the next day'. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein 'kindly' retain hai aur 'tomorrow' unshifted hai. Option (C) mein 'requested to the superintendent' incorrect preposition leta hai. Option (D) subordinate to superior context mein inappropriate 'ordered' verb use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Request conversion with polite drop and adverbial shifts.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the warning into Indirect Speech:
The court master said to the audience, "Do not record the video of the court proceedings."

options.text: The court master warned the audience to not record the video of the court proceedings.
The court master warned the audience not to record the video of the court proceedings.
The court master forbade the audience not to record the video of the court proceedings.
The court master ordered the audience that do not record the video of the court proceedings.

questions.explanation: Warning context mein reporting verb 'warned' aayegi aur negative command 'Do not + V1' badal kar 'not to + V1' ('not to record') banega. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) split infinitive 'to not record' use karta hai jo exam standards mein second choice maana jata hai. Option (C) mein fatal double negative 'forbade... not to' blunder hai. Option (D) imperative mein declarative 'that do not' structure use karta hai jo completely ungrammatical hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Negative imperative structure 'warned + object + not to + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Which of the following represents an accurate Indirect Speech conversion of:
The officer said to the staff, "Never share your system assistant login passwords with anyone."

options.text: The officer forbade the staff not to share their system assistant login passwords with anyone.
The officer forbade the staff to ever share their system assistant login passwords with anyone.
The officer told the staff to never share your system assistant login passwords with anyone.
The officer ordered the staff that they should never share their system assistant login passwords with anyone.

questions.explanation: 'Forbade' negative verb hai, isliye 'Never' ka negative sense 'forbade' mein absorb ho jata hai aur subordinate clause positive polarity ('to ever share') follow karta hai. 2nd person 'your' staff ke anusaar 'their' ban gaya. Option (B) bilkul flawless aur advanced construction hai. Option (A) mein 'forbade... not to' double negative hai. Option (C) mein pronoun 'your' unshifted hai aur split infinitive hai. Option (D) unnecessarily long declarative construction hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Forbade absorbs negative polarity ('never' becomes positive infinitive with 'ever').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the proposal into Indirect Speech:
Rohan said to his co-workers, "Let's resolve this network glitch before lunch."

options.text: Rohan ordered his co-workers to resolve this network glitch before lunch.
Rohan suggested to his co-workers that they should resolve that network glitch before lunch.
Rohan suggested his co-workers that they resolve that network glitch before lunch.
Rohan proposed his co-workers to resolve that network glitch before lunch.

questions.explanation: 'Let's' mutual suggestion ya proposal express karta hai, isliye reporting verb 'suggested to his co-workers' lagti hai (preposition 'to' mandatory hai). Conjunction 'that' lagta hai aur modal 'should' ke sath 'they should resolve' banta hai. Demonstrative 'this' ➔ 'that' convert hota hai. Option (B) 100% correct hai. Option (A) proposal ko command bana deta hai. Option (C) mein 'suggested' ke baad preposition 'to' drop kar diya gaya hai ('suggested his co-workers'). Option (D) non-standard infinitive pattern use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: 'Let's' proposals require 'suggested to + object + that they should + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the exclamatory sentence into Indirect Speech:
The successful candidates said, "Hurrah! We have cleared the High Court System Assistant examination!"

options.text: The successful candidates exclaimed with joy that they had cleared the High Court System Assistant examination.
The successful candidates exclaimed with sorrow that they had cleared the High Court System Assistant examination.
The successful candidates exclaimed with joy that we had cleared the High Court System Assistant examination.
The successful candidates said that Hurrah they cleared the High Court System Assistant examination.

questions.explanation: Interjection 'Hurrah!' joy aur celebration express karta hai, isliye reporting phrase 'exclaimed with joy' banega aur 'Hurrah!' drop ho jayega. Conjunction 'that' aayega. 1st person plural 'We' candidates ke anusaar 'they' banega, aur Present Perfect 'have cleared' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had cleared' banega. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) inappropriate emotion 'sorrow' use karta hai. Option (C) mein pronoun 'we' unshifted chhod diya gaya hai. Option (D) interjection 'Hurrah' ko quoted word ki tarah retain karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Exclamatory with 'Hurrah!' converts to 'exclaimed with joy that...'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Exclamatory Sentence with 'What a / How' Intensifier Conversion
questions.question:
Convert into Indirect Speech:
The junior lawyer said, "What an intricate legal precedent the Chief Justice delivered!"

options.text: The junior lawyer exclaimed that what an intricate legal precedent the Chief Justice had delivered.
The junior lawyer exclaimed with admiration that the Chief Justice had delivered a very intricate legal precedent.
The junior lawyer said that the Chief Justice delivered a very intricate legal precedent.
The junior lawyer exclaimed with wonder that did the Chief Justice deliver an intricate legal precedent.

questions.explanation: 'What an intricate legal precedent...!' admiration aur wonder express karta hai. Indirect speech mein sentence assertive statement banta hai: 'What a' drop hokar intensity convey karne ke liye adjective se pehle 'very' jud jata hai ('a very intricate legal precedent'). Simple Past 'delivered' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had delivered' ban jata hai. Option (B) bilkul flawless hai. Option (A) exclamatory syntax 'what an intricate' ko retain karta hai. Option (C) emotion completely omit kar deta hai aur backshift nahi karta. Option (D) statement ko interrogative inversion bana deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'What a / How' exclamations convert to assertive statements with 'very/great'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Choose the most accurate Indirect Speech conversion:
The presiding judge said to the young advocate, "Bravo! You argued the writ petition exceptionally well!"

options.text: The presiding judge applauded the young advocate saying that he had argued the writ petition exceptionally well.
The presiding judge exclaimed with joy that the young advocate argued the writ petition exceptionally well.
The presiding judge said Bravo to the young advocate that he had argued the writ petition exceptionally well.
The presiding judge applauded to the young advocate that he argued the writ petition exceptionally well.

questions.explanation: Interjection 'Bravo!' praise aur applause express karta hai. Standard examination reporting formula: 'applauded + object + saying that + subject + had + V3' hota hai. Simple Past 'argued' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had argued' banega. Option (A) bilkul standard aur accurate hai. Option (B) personal commendation ko generic joy mein dilute kar deta hai aur tense backshift omit karta hai. Option (C) crude ungrammatical conversion hai. Option (D) 'applauded to' incorrect preposition aur unbackshifted tense use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: 'Bravo!' converts to 'applauded + object + saying that...'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the optative sentence into Indirect Speech:
The mentor said to the apprentice, "May you achieve excellence in your judicial service career!"

options.text: The mentor wished that the apprentice might achieve excellence in his judicial service career.
The mentor wished that might the apprentice achieve excellence in his judicial service career.
The mentor prayed to the apprentice to achieve excellence in your judicial service career.
The mentor wished that the apprentice may achieve excellence in his judicial service career.

questions.explanation: General well-wish ke liye reporting verb 'wished' lagti hai. Conjunction 'that' ke baad subject 'the apprentice' aayega, aur modal 'May' backshift hokar 'might' banega jo subject ke BAAD aayega ('that the apprentice might achieve'). 2nd person 'your' ➔ 'his' banega. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) mein inverted order 'might the apprentice' retain hai. Option (C) apprentice se prayer kar raha hai jo contextually absurd hai. Option (D) mein 'may' ko 'might' mein backshift nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Optative wishes with 'that + Subject + might + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Select the correct Indirect form of the farewell statement:
The retired registrar said to his colleagues, "Farewell, my friends! May prosperity follow you all!"

options.text: The retired registrar bade his friends farewell and wished that prosperity might follow them all.
The retired registrar said farewell to his friends and prayed that may prosperity follow them all.
The retired registrar wished farewell to his friends and prayed that might prosperity follow them all.
The retired registrar bade farewell his friends and wished that prosperity follows them all.

questions.explanation: Alvida (farewell) kehne ke liye verb 'bade' (past of bid) use hoti hai: 'bade his friends farewell'. Uske baad jude optative clause ke liye reporting verb 'wished' aayegi aur 'May prosperity follow' statement syntax mein 'that prosperity might follow them all' banega. Option (A) dono clauses ko flawlessly report karta hai. Option (B) 'said farewell' informal hai aur unbackshifted 'may' use karta hai. Option (C) inverted modal 'might prosperity' use karta hai. Option (D) syntax error aur unbackshifted 'follows' contain karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Farewell greetings require 'bade + object + farewell' and optative might clause.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07
